comparison: Both evaluate the nanobody generation methodology and repertoire diversity (C27-C41). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 1A-C and detailed methods. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, praising 'an impressive collection of hundreds of new nanobodies' with no concerns about pipeline methodology. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate binding characterization and affinity data (C42-C51). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by SPR data in Figure 2 and Tables 1-2. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'comprehensive characterization' with only minor requests for clarification on normalization methods. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate variant binding data (C53-C56). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by SPR data in Figure 2G and Table 3. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, accepting the data but suggesting expansion to include Delta variant. Strong agreement on data validity.

Both evaluate thermal stability and lyophilization data (C57-C58). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by DSF data and experiments in Figure 2D-F. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED as part of 'comprehensive characterization' with no concerns raised. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate epitope binning and simultaneous binding (C59-C62). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by biolayer interferometry and mass photometry data. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging the work 'defines epitopes on the RBD or spike' with requests for additional context. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate pseudovirus neutralization including non-RBD nanobodies (C63-C69). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 4A-C data. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, praising identification of 'non-receptor binding domain nanobodies' as significant, with requests for benchmark comparisons. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate oligomerization and potency enhancement (C70-C75). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 4D-F and Table 4. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'extensive bioengineering to substantially improve potency' with citation requests. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate SARS-CoV-1 cross-neutralization (C76-C79). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 4K and Table 5. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, contributing to overall assessment of 'significant impacts on SARS-CoV-2 research.' Strong agreement.

Both evaluate authentic virus neutralization and ALI culture data (C80-C83). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 5A, Table 6, and Figure 5C. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED with minor presentation clarification requested about ALI model description. Strong agreement on data validity.

Both evaluate escape mutant selection and cocktail resistance (C84-C88). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Table 7 and Figure 6 supplement data. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, praising demonstration of 'resistance to escaping variants' with citation requests. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate integrative modeling of nanobody-spike complexes (C89-C93). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 6 with appropriate caveats about resolution. Peer reviewers find UNCERTAIN, expressing concern about reliance on IMP modeling without validation using a structurally characterized nanobody as control. Significant disagreement on confidence in modeling approach.

Both address epitope mapping and coverage (C94-C97). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by neutralization data across multiple figures. Peer reviewers find UNCERTAIN due to concerns about IMP modeling validation (overlapping with R17 concerns). Disagreement stems from modeling methodology concerns.

Both address S2-targeting neutralizing nanobodies (C98). OpenEval finds claim SUPPORTED as a novel finding with structural mapping. Peer reviewers find UNCERTAIN due to concerns about IMP modeling validation used for structural mapping. Disagreement on confidence in structural characterization.

Both evaluate synergy data and nanobody cocktails (C99-C104). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 7, Table 9, and multiple synergy models. Peer reviewers find UNCERTAIN, questioning whether synergy is unique to nanobodies vs IgG antibodies, noting the 2D response assay is not well-adopted, and expressing confusion about the >4000-fold increase claim. Significant disagreement on interpretation and uniqueness of findings.
